_doc: Infantry loading and firing drill as printed in Casey's Infantry Tactics (1862, Van Nostrand; vol. 1 = Schools of the Soldier and Company and Skirmishers; vol. 2 = School of the Battalion), with cartridge/cap/buck-and-ball statements from the Ordnance Manual (Richmond 1861 reprint of the US text) and Gibbon. Every item has manual id, printed page (recovered from OCR running heads; confidence stated), a verbatim OCR phrase verified by tools/bt/drill_check.py, and a paraphrase. Hardee's text was acquired afterwards: see drill_hardee.json and drill_compare.json for the Hardee-vs-Casey comparison. All items tier=documented (primary manual text, OCR-verified); the OCR is raw and uncorrected.

load_in_nine_times.where: School of the Soldier, Part II, Lesson II, paras 163-177
load_in_nine_times.note: Nine "times" (commands of execution); draw rammer and return rammer have three motions each, prime and shoulder arms two. The manual does not use the word "ready" or "fire" in the nine.

load_in_eight_times.note: Maynard-primer variant only; a table of its other times is not printed in this passage.

hardee_vs_casey.status: SUPERSEDED - Hardee acquired (HARDEE-1861a, HARDEE-1861b in acquired.json); the item-by-item comparison is drill_compare.json, the Hardee passages are drill_hardee.json, notes in DRILL-HARDEE-NOTES.md
hardee_vs_casey.history: When this file was first built no Hardee text was available: the three named manuals (Casey vol 1, Casey vol 2, Gibbon, Ordnance Manual) contain no Hardee text and the one allowed extra fetch went to the artillery drill manual. Hardee was downloaded later.

what_casey_itself_says.paraphrase: Casey's preface (dated 1 Jan 1862) says the volumes are based on the French ordonnances of 1831 and 1845, the latter translated by Hardee, and that few changes from the original were made in the schools of vol. 1. That supports 'same lineage, few changes' for the loading drill; the comparison with Hardee's own text (drill_compare.json) confirms it.

pdf_claim_checks.claim: PDF B.6.11: nine commands "load; handle cartridge; tear cartridge; charge cartridge; draw rammer; ram cartridge; return rammer; prime; shoulder arms" (memory, unverified)
pdf_claim_checks.verdict: CONFIRMED (exact list and order) for Casey 1862
pdf_claim_checks.caveat: Confirmed for Casey here; Hardee prints the same nine commands, order and motions (drill_hardee.json HAR-S02..S10, drill_compare.json CMP-S02..S10).

pdf_claim_checks.claim: PDF: nine-step muzzle-loader drill against five for breech-loaders (ABT-SmallArms)
pdf_claim_checks.verdict: nine for muzzle-loader CONFIRMED (Casey); the five-step breech-loader count is not in these texts

pdf_claim_checks.claim: PDF forum claim: in combat only eight cycles occur because the ninth step (return to shoulder) occurs only on the first load
pdf_claim_checks.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED as stated by Casey; Casey has the loader come back to shoulder arms as time 9 and, after firing, uses "Load" to return to the loading position (para 186). The ninth time is the "shoulder arms" at the end of loading, which a man firing continuously (ready-aim-fire-load) does not need between rounds; the manual does not say so explicitly. Treat the forum claim as unconfirmed.

pdf_claim_checks.claim: PDF rate: 2-3 rounds a minute typical (M1861)
pdf_claim_checks.verdict: Casey states 3 rounds a minute as a minimum drill standard (S.C. para 47); consistent with the 2-3 range as an upper end

pdf_claim_checks.claim: PDF: each ten cartridges came with twelve caps
pdf_claim_checks.verdict: NOT SETTLED: Ordnance Manual OCR of the cap count is unreadable

pdf_claim_checks.claim: PDF: buck and ball good at 50 yd
pdf_claim_checks.verdict: The Ordnance Manual documents the buck-and-ball cartridge (ball + 3 buckshot; 4 tiers of 3 for the all-buckshot cartridge) but gives no effective range in the passages found
No misfire RATES in these texts; Casey gives only the misfire PROCEDURE (pick and prime; double-loading check)

items.paraphrase: Time 9 "Shoulder arms" (one time, two motions): piece brought to the right shoulder and supported by the left hand, face to the front, right heel brought to the left; right hand takes the shoulder-arms grasp; left hand dropped quickly to the side.

items.paraphrase: "Ready" (one time, three motions): raise the piece, half face right, right foot to the rear; bring the piece down with both hands, barrel up, butt below the right forearm, muzzle at eye height, left elbow against the side; right thumb to the cock; third motion cocks the piece and re-seizes the small of the stock.

items.paraphrase: "Aim": piece raised with both hands, butt against the right shoulder, left elbow down, right elbow as high as the shoulder, head inclined on the butt, right eye to the sight, left eye closed, finger on the trigger.
